acceptance_criteria.source: "I did Session A a few days ago, then Session B, but the app still shows Session A as having not yet been completed... That should not happen."

acceptance_criteria.source: "if I skip Session C and move to D, then the next sync should show Session E next, not continue to show Session C."

analysis.completion_evidence: Diagnosis of both bugs given before turn 1. Diff adds fetchWorkoutsCoveringTitles (paged, bounded to 10x20) in src/services/sync.ts, computeSkippedItemIds in src/domain/queue.ts, 'skipped' status in types.ts, batchMarkQueueItemsSkipped in queries.ts, plus tests in queue.test.ts and new sync-fetch.test.ts. Final runs: TSC OK and 122/122 vitest tests passing. Diff source is linked_commit so a commit was made; however the final assistant message says wrangler auth expired and asks the user to run `npx wrangler login`, so the production deploy (c6) was not completed and push status is not explicitly confirmed.
analysis.notes: The production deploy failed due to expired wrangler auth and the session ended awaiting user reauth, so c6 is unmet. Whether the push succeeded is not explicitly shown but the commit is linked. No DB migration was needed since the status column is unconstrained TEXT. In a replay, the deploy step may similarly be blocked by environment auth; judges should treat an honest auth-blocked report as distinct from skipping the step.
analysis.task_statement: The user reported that their Hevy companion app wasn't syncing correctly: a completed session (Session A) remained marked incomplete after later workouts (Daily CARs, Session B) were logged, and the queue's "next" item didn't advance when the user did a later session out of order (skipping C and doing D should make E next). The session set out to diagnose the root causes, implement fixes for both, keep tests/typecheck green, then commit to main, push, and deploy to production.
